description.narrative:
Media Institute Fojo has applied to the Embassy for funding of MSEK 72 to carry out the "Rwanda Media Programme 2021-25 , Capacity Building and Professionalisation of the Media". The programme will be implemented in partnership with Swedish Radio Media Development Office (SR MDO).
The objective of the contribution is to strengthen the independence, professionalism, and sustainability of key actors in the Rwandan media sector with the aim to increase media diversity and media integrity. This in turn will contribute to increase the population's access to independent, trustworthy, impartial news and information through the media as a platform for citizen's participation and interaction. The programme activities are divided under three Outcome areas, (1) capacity development of targeted media houses on journalistic capacity, management and financial sustainability, (2) capacity development of Rwanda Broadcasting Agency (RBA) in line with the principles of public service media, and (3) strengthening journalist education in targeted universities.
The intervention's total budget is MSEK 78,3, out of which Sida will contribute with MSEK 72 and Swizz Development Cooperation with the part (USD 800 000). Approximately MSEK 32 will be forwarded from Fojo to SR MDO, and about MSEK 14 from Fojo to local implementing partners.

Mediainstitutet Fojo has ansökt om 72 miljoner kronor i stöd för att genomföra insatsen "Rwanda Media Programme 2021-25, Capacity Building and Professionalisation of the Media" mellan mars 2021 och februari 2026. Insatsen genomförs i samarbete med Swedish Radio Media Development Office (SR MDO).
Insatsens mål är att stärka oberoende, professionalism och hållbarhet hos media med syftet att öka en mångfald och integritet i mediasektorn. Detta i sin tur ska bidra till att öka befolkningens tillgång till oberoende och pålitliga nyheter och information genom media och att media på så sätt kan fungera som en plattform för ansvarsutkrävande och medborgerligt deltagande. Programmet är uppdelat i tre resultatområden med specifika mål och aktiviteter, (1) kapacitetsstärkande av utvalda mediahus kring journalistisk kapacitet, management och finansiell hållbarhet, (2) kapacitetsstärkande av Rwanda Broadcasting Agency (RBA) i linje med public service-principer, and (3) stärka journalistutbildningen i utvalda universitet.
Insatsens sammalagda budget är 78,3 miljoner kronor, av vilken Sida finansierar 72 MSEK, och resterande belopp finansieras av den schweitziska ambassaden (800 000 USD). Cirka 32 MSEK kommer vidareförmedlas till SR MDO och ca 14 MSEK till lokala samarbetpartners.

The Overall objective is that the Rwandan people access independent, trustworthy, impartial news and information through the media as a platform for citizens participation and interaction.
The specific objective is strengthening the independence, professionalism, and sustainability of key actors in the Rwandan media sector with the aim to increase media diversity and media integrity.
Outcome 1: Commercial and non-profit media are strengthened to become financially sustainable and to produce and disseminate public interest journalism, reflecting the full composition of society through a balanced presence of women and men, age groups and communities.
Outcome 3: Journalism education institutions have increased skills concerning practical journalism, awareness of gender issues, and are better connected with the Rwandan media and the international journalism community.
The original outcome 2 was formulated as: RBA is strengthened in the process to become an independent, trustworthy and sustainable Public Service Media (PSM) provider according to international journalistic and public service standards. This outcome has been discontinued early 2025 on the initiative of the implementing partner SR MDO. The contribution, hence, remains with the outcome 1 and 3.

title.narrative: Decision on Amendment on Contribution Rwanda Media Programme 2021-2025

description.narrative:
As was described last year, the programme operates in two outcome areas after the premature closure of public service and the cooperation between SR MDO and RBA (outcome 2). Since the last conclusion of performance, the programme has achieved a number of results, some of which were reported in the recent annual report. Some examples of results are mentioned below.
Outcome 1 Media Sustainability and Inclusivity
During 2025, the private and independent media component demonstrated a high level of maturity, as interventions successfully shifted from ad-hoc routines to structured editorial systems. A total of seven major media houses managed to reform their daily operational procedures, which manifested in concrete milestones such as redesigned websites, strengthened multimedia production capacities, and the comprehensive adoption of modern digital workflows. This digital and structural transition has been heavily driven by the programme's focus on audience-centric business models. In practice, this means that media houses transitioned from intuitive or ad-hoc content creation to utilizing empirical data, for example from the national consumption surveys. By aligning their digital platforms and investigative journalism with the verified preferences and behaviors of their audience, they enhanced their capacity to attract external investors. The two National Media Consumption Surveys (the last in 2024) continued to generate substantial industry-wide impact; an increasing number of newsrooms now actively utilize this audience data to guide their daily editorial decisions, which in turn has significantly improved their capacity to attract commercial advertisers.
In the realm of investigative and special reporting, participating journalists demonstrated a stronger application of core journalistic principles. Several of the published investigations were highly impactful, directly leading to concrete institutional actions and public accountability. Over the recent years, Fojo has systematically and successfully expanded the operational space and capacity for media houses to engage in professional investigative journalism. This structural advancement has reached a point where high-quality investigative reporting is not only tolerated but actively sought after and requested by state and regulatory actors such as the Rwanda Governance Board (RGB) and the Rwanda Media Commission (RMC).
This rigorous focus on quality went hand in hand with the programme's gender and environmental work. The collaboration within the network of female journalist associations (Synergy of female journalist associations) grew noticeably in terms of professionalism and external public trust, while internal anti-harassment and gender policies implemented within the partner media houses were substantially improved. Concurrently, environmental journalists produced stories that directly influenced government action, most notably contributing to a major policy breakthrough resulting in a Rwf 3.9 billion state budget allocation specifically designated for hazardous waste management.
Finally, the long-term sustainability of the intervention has been reinforced through the significant capacity development of the local Rwanda Media Programme team. Over the course of the year, the local staff members have grown into independent experts and trainers in their own right. As a powerful testament to this localized knowledge transfer and regional relevance, one of the Rwandan team members was officially engaged to serve as a specialized trainer in two other African countries during the last year.
Outcome 3 Enhanced Journalism Education
Within the academic component of the programme, the primary focus during 2025 was on securing sustainable student media and practical skills. The four student-led magazines established under the intervention are now publishing daily content and have achieved full institutional ownership by the universities themselves. This transition of ownership represents a crucial milestone, ensuring that daily content production will continue independently beyond the lifecycle of the programme. Students gained invaluable practical tools through targeted training sessions in mobile journalism, which were effectively combined with continuous editorial mentorship and professional internships. This strong bridge to the media industry bore immediate fruit during the year, as several former student interns transitioned directly into paid professional employment within the media sector upon graduation.
One of the most significant structural and institutional advancements of the year was the establishment of national academic networks. Supported directly by RMP, the Rwanda Journalism Educators' Network (RJEN) was formally and legally established in 2025. This marks the first national platform of its kind in Rwanda where journalism educators, lecturers, and researchers can systematically collaborate, exchange pedagogical best practices, and jointly address cross-cutting sectoral challenges.
The institutional gender work at the four partner universities also continued to yield robust results. Student-led gender clubs became increasingly self-driven and autonomous during the year, launching localized activities aimed explicitly at increasing women's representation in student governance and university leadership bodies. At the curricular level, specialized gender modules were introduced on a broad front, officially integrated at both the bachelor's and master's degree levels across all four participating universities. On an overarching institutional level, the universities now report stronger, more modern teaching practices and a significantly more practice-oriented curriculum, with several of the higher education institutions having begun the formal process of embedding these qualitative changes into their own internal quality assurance mechanisms and official course registries.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
